turns.query: Create a retrospective revision screen for annualized real GDP growth from 2024-Q1 through 2025-Q2. Retain only quarters with first, second, third and current estimates, rank them by the absolute current-minus-first revision, and break a tie by the earlier quarter. Report the retained-quarter count, selected quarter, its first and current rates, and the selected absolute revision minus the runner-up absolute revision. Briefly explain how the selected retrospective revision magnitude should be interpreted.

For that selected quarter, report the second and third estimates. Among the three adjacent changes (second minus first, third minus second, current minus third), identify the stage with the largest absolute change, using the earliest transition in the stated sequence to break a tie. Explain whether the final revision was accumulated uniformly across release stages.

Carry the selected quarter into a rates-market window. Use the most recent reported Treasury par-yield-curve observation on or before the preceding calendar-quarter end and the most recent one on or before the selected quarter end. Report both observation dates; the 2-year and 10-year yields at each boundary; and the 10-year-minus-2-year spread at each boundary. Interpret the curve-shape change with appropriate temporal calibration to the release-vintage evidence.

Finally, for the CFTC futures-only U.S. Treasury 2-year and 10-year note contracts, use the latest report on or before each of the two quarter boundaries from the prior turn. Report the two CFTC dates. For each contract report leveraged-money long minus short at both boundaries, ending minus starting net contracts, and net as a percentage of that contract's same-report open interest at both boundaries. Compare the two positioning paths, but explain the contract-scale and causal limits of relating them to the curve and GDP-revision evidence.
